note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Decode-phase bottlenecks and sparse-attention dilemmas lead to FFD's design and its efficiency/accuracy results

nodes.name: Decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound
nodes.description: In the autoregressive decode phase each token generation reloads the entire KV cache from HBM, so IO rather than FLOPs is the primary bottleneck, creating a memory wall for long contexts.

nodes.name: Selector-Computer separation wastes computation
nodes.description: In the standard decoupled Selector-Computer paradigm, the computer cannot reuse the selector's intermediate computations, creating efficiency bottlenecks.

nodes.name: Metric dilemma
nodes.description: Importance metrics that rely on extra metadata (partial dimensions, centroids, geometric bounds) either incur additional memory overhead or suffer information distortion.

nodes.name: Selection dilemma
nodes.description: Top-k selection is cheap but cannot adapt to varying attention entropy, while top-p adapts to the distribution but needs a global softmax and sorting, which adds overhead and breaks the streaming pipeline.

nodes.name: Content-aware 2-bit scanning
nodes.description: FFD splits the K cache into a 2-bit quantized thumbnail for scanning and an 8-bit residual for refinement (symmetric zero-free mid-rise quantization), replacing metadata-based indexing and avoiding metadata memory overhead.

nodes.name: Top-delta rule
nodes.description: Top-delta keeps tokens with score s_ij at least m_i minus delta, i.e. attention at least e^-delta of the peak; delta=5 discards only tokens below about 0.67% of peak attention mass.

nodes.name: Pseudo-max avoids global reduction
nodes.description: Estimating the maximum score from only sink and local tokens (pseudo-max), justified by attention being dominated by sink and local tokens, lets the threshold be computed locally so KV blocks are processed independently without global synchronization.

nodes.name: Pseudo-max approximation is accurate
nodes.description: The gap between true max and pseudo-max is below 0.01 in 86.1% of cases, so the approximation is a robust safe relaxation.

nodes.name: Fused kernel with refinement and CUDA graphs
nodes.description: FFD runs pseudo-max estimation, 2-bit top-delta selection and 8-bit refinement as fused Triton kernels reusing the scan, and uses full-chain block-wise JIT CUDA graphs that run 99% of decode steps within a graph.

nodes.name: Top-delta selection is cheaper than top-k and top-p
nodes.description: At a matched keep ratio of about 27.3%, top-delta selection is 2x faster than top-k and 25x faster than top-p.

nodes.name: Kernel speedup up to 11.6x
nodes.description: On an RTX 4090 FFD kernel latency scales linearly with a much lower slope than FlashAttention-2, with average speedups of 7.33x (delta=5) and 6.18x (delta=7) and a peak of 11.63x; at 256K it is 0.17 ms versus 1.12 ms.

nodes.name: End-to-end throughput gains
nodes.description: FFD reaches up to 2.37x throughput over FlashAttention-2 at 16K on RTX 4090 (51.8 vs Quest 47.8 tokens/s) and 1.96x on H100 (87.0 vs 44.5 tokens/s).

nodes.name: KIVI underperforms dense attention
nodes.description: KIVI is slower than dense attention in the low-batch regime (22.4 vs 44.5 tokens/s on H100 at 16K) because of dequantization cost.

nodes.name: RULER accuracy preserved
nodes.description: On RULER at 32K with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, FFD matches the dense baseline on NIAH single-key tasks (100.0) and has minimal degradation on Variable Tracking (98.4 vs 99.6).

nodes.name: Adaptive top-delta handles multi-peak retrieval
nodes.description: Fixed-budget Quest drops sharply on MK-3 (6.0) whereas FFD with top-delta reaches 95.0, and FFD consistently outperforms Twilight on both benchmarks.

nodes.name: LongBench result
nodes.description: On LongBench (21 datasets, 6 categories) FFD with delta=7 achieves the highest overall average of 26.35 among compared methods.

nodes.name: Higher recall than Quest
nodes.description: FFD achieves higher recall and lower LSE error than Quest at the same retrieval budget, and maintains higher Spearman correlation across layers, because 2-bit quantization preserves key directionality better than min/max bounds.

nodes.name: Fusion and 2-bit scanning are synergistic
nodes.description: The fused 2-bit top-delta configuration achieves 53.96 tok/s, RULER AVG 90.40 and LongBench AVG 25.90, a 2.2x throughput gain over its split-execution counterpart.

nodes.name: Generalizes to Qwen2.5
nodes.description: On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with delta=7, FFD gets RULER AVG 85.90 and LongBench AVG 30.11, outperforming KIVI, Quest and StreamingLLM.

isolated_nodes.name: Quest memory footprint matched
isolated_nodes.description: Quest with page size 16 has index memory footprint equal to FFD's 2-bit data for full scanning, with token budget aligned at 16k, making the comparison fair.

isolated_nodes.name: Delta=7 is conservative
isolated_nodes.description: delta=7 corresponds to threshold e^-7 (about 1/1096), retaining tokens with about 0.1% relative importance, a conservative setting versus the aggressive delta=5 targeting the top ~1% tokens.

structural_reasoning: Problem diagnosis (memory wall, metric and selection dilemmas) leads to the design components (2-bit scanning, top-delta, pseudo-max), fused into a kernel, which then underpins efficiency and accuracy results. Setup facts isolated.
